# Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision

## This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 52

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 52] Contents of this Practice Direction

## Contents of this Practice Direction

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Contents of this Practice Direction] This Practice Direction is divided into the following sections:

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section I –Introduction

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section II – Routes of appeal

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section III – General provisions about statutory appeals

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section IV – Specific appeals

## SECTION I – INTRODUCTION

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > SECTION I – INTRODUCTION] 1.1 This Practice Direction applies to all statutory appeals, and to other appeals which are subject to special provision, but not to appeals by way of case stated (to which Practice Direction 52E applies). ## SECTION II – ROUTES OF APPEAL

## 2.1 In this Practice Direction, the court to which an appeal lies is prescribed by statute. ## SECTION III – GENERAL PROVISIONS ABOUT STATUTORY APPEALS

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > SECTION III – GENERAL PROVISIONS ABOUT STATUTORY APPEALS] 3.1 This Section contains general provisions about statutory appeals (paragraphs 3.2 – 3.8). For where this Practice Direction or a statute makes additional special provision see also Section 4. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > SECTION III – GENERAL PROVISIONS ABOUT STATUTORY APPEALS] 3.2 Where any of the provisions in this Section provide for documents to be filed at the appeal court, those documents are in addition to any documents required under Part 52 or Practice Direction 52B or 52C. ## 3.3

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 3.3] Subject to rule 52.9—

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 3.3] Where the appellant wishes to appeal against a decision of the Upper Tribunal, the appellant’s notice must be filed within 28 days of the date on which notice of the Upper Tribunal’s decision on permission to appeal to the Court of Appeal is sent to the appellant. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 3.3] 3.3A Where a statement of reasons for a decision is given later than the notice of that decision, the period for filing the appellant’s notice is calculated from the date on which the statement is sent to the appellant. ## Service of appellant’s notice: rule 52.12(3)

## 3.4

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 3.4] (1) The appellant must serve the appellant’s notice on the respondent and on the chairman of the tribunal, Minister of State, government department or other person from whose decision the appeal is brought. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 3.4] (2) In the case of an appeal from the decision of a tribunal that has no chairman or member who acts as a chairman, the appellant’s notice must be served on the member (or members if more than one) of the tribunal. ## Variation of time: rule 52.15

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Variation of time: rule 52.15] 3.5 Where any statute prescribes a period within which an appeal must be filed then, unless the statute otherwise provides, the appeal court may not extend that period. ## Applications by third parties (rule 52.25)

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Applications by third parties (rule 52.25)] 3.6 Where all the parties consent, the court may deal with an application under rule 52.12A without a hearing. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Applications by third parties (rule 52.25)] 3.7 An application for permission must be made by letter to the relevant court office, identifying the appeal, explaining who the applicant is and indicating why and in what form the applicant wants to participate in the hearing. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Applications by third parties (rule 52.25)] 3.8 If the applicant is seeking a prospective order as to costs, the letter must say what kind of order and on what grounds. ## SECTION IV – SPECIFIC APPEALS

## Provisions about specific appeals

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Provisions about specific appeals] 4.1 This Section sets out special provisions about the appeals listed in the Table below. This Section is not exhaustive and does not create, amend or remove any right of appeal. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Provisions about specific appeals] 4.2 Part 52 applies to all appeals to which this Section applies subject to any special provisions set out in this Section. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Provisions about specific appeals] 4.3 Where any of the provisions in this Section provide for documents to be filed at the appeal court, these documents are in addition to any documents required under Part 52 or Practice Direction 52B or 52C. ## Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] 5.1 Any appeal to the High Court, and any case stated or question referred for the opinion of that court under any of the following enactments shall be heard in the Chancery Division –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] (1) section 38(3) of the Clergy Pensions Measure 1961;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] (2) Omitted

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] (3) the Industrial and Provident Societies Act 1965;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] (4) section 222(3) of the Inheritance Tax Act 1984;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] (5) the Land Registration Act 2002;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] (6) paragraph 16 of Schedule 15 to the Law of Property Act 1922;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] (7) section 215 or 217 of the Pensions Act 2004;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] (8) section 151 of the Pension Schemes Act 1993;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] (9) section 13 and 13B of the Stamp Act 1891;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] (10) regulation 8(3) of the Stamp Duty Reserve Tax Regulations 1986. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division] Table

## APPEALS TO THE COURT OF APPEAL

## 6.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (1) The appellant must file the appellant’s notice at the Court of Appeal within 28 days after the date on which the decree was pronounced or conditional order made. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (2) The appellant must file the following documents with the appellant’s notice –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (a) the decree or conditional order; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (b) a certificate of service of the appellant’s notice. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (3) The appellant’s notice must be served on the appropriate District Judge (see sub-paragraph (6)) in addition to the persons to be served under rule 52.12(3) and in accordance with that rule. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (4) The lower court may not alter the time limits for filing of the appeal notices. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (5) Where an appellant intends to apply to the Court of Appeal for an extension of time for serving or filing the appellant’s notice the appellant must give notice of that intention to the appropriate District Judge (see sub-paragraph 6) before the application is made. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (6) In this paragraph ‘the appropriate District Judge’ means, where the lower court is –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (a) the County Court, the District Judge of the County Court hearing centre in question;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (b) a district registry, the District Judge of that registry;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (c) the Principal Registry of the Family Division, the senior District Judge of that division. ## 7.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (1) This paragraph applies to any appeal to the Court of Appeal relating to the application Chapter I or Chapter II of Part I of the Competition Act 1998. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (2) In this paragraph –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (a) ‘the 1988 Act’ means the Competition Act 1998 or to a claim under section 101 of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (aa) ‘the 2024 Act’ means the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (b) Omitted

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (c) Omitted

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (d) “competition “authority” means —

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (i) the Competition and Markets Authority; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (ii) a regulator as defined in section 54 of the 1988 Act;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (e) Omitted

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (3) Any party whose appeal notice raises an issue relating to the application of Chapter I or II of Part I of the 1998 Act or to a claim under section 101 of the 2024 Act, must –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (a) state that fact in the appeal notice; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (b) serve a copy of the appeal notice on the Competition and Markets Authority (addressed to the General Counsel, the Competition and Markets Authority, The Cabot, 25 Cabot Square, London, E14 4QZ. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (4) Omitted

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (5) A  competition authority may make written observations to the Court of Appeal, or apply for permission to make oral observations, on issues relating to the application of Chapter I or II of the 1998 Act. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (5A) The Competition and Markets Authority may make written observations to the Court of Appeal, or apply for permission to make oral observations, on issues relating to a claim under section 101 of the 2024 Act. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (6) If a competition authority intends to make written observations to the Court of Appeal, it must give notice of its intention to do so by letter to the Civil Appeals Office at the earliest opportunity. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (7) An application by a competition authority for permission to make oral representations at the hearing of an appeal must be made by letter to the Civil Appeals Office at the earliest opportunity, identifying the appeal and indicating why the applicant wishes to make oral representations. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (8) If a competition authority files a notice under sub-paragraph (6) or an application under sub-paragraph (7), it must at the same time serve a copy of the notice or application on every party to the appeal. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (9) Any request by a competition authority for the court to send it any documents relating to an appeal should be made at the same time as filing a notice under sub-paragraph (6) or an application under sub-paragraph (7). [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (10) When the Court of Appeal receives a notice under sub-paragraph (6) it may give case management directions to the competition authority, including directions about the date by which any written observations are to be filed. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (11) The Court of Appeal will serve on every party to the appeal a copy of any directions given or order made–

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (a) on an application under sub-paragraph (7); or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (b) under sub-paragraph (10). ## Appeal from Competition Appeal Tribunal

## 8.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 8.1] (1) Where the appellant applies for permission to appeal at the hearing at which the decision is delivered by the tribunal and –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 8.1] (a) permission is given; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 8.1] (b) permission is refused and the appellant wishes to make an application to the Court of Appeal for permission to appeal,

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 8.1] the appellant’s notice must be filed at the Court of Appeal within 14 days after the date of that hearing. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 8.1] (2) Where the appellant applies in writing to the Registrar of the tribunal for permission to appeal and–

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 8.1] (a) permission is given; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 8.1] (b) permission is refused and the appellant wishes to make an application to the Court of Appeal for permission to appeal,

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 8.1] the appellant’s notice must be filed at the Court of Appeal within 14 days after the date of receipt of the tribunal’s decision on permission. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 8.1] (3) Where the appellant does not make an application to the tribunal for permission to appeal, but wishes to make an application to the Court of Appeal for permission, the appellant’s notice must be filed at the Court of Appeal within 14 days after the end of the period within which the appellant may make a written application to the Registrar of the tribunal. ## Appeals in cases of contempt of court (section 13 Administration of Justice Act 1960)

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Appeals in cases of contempt of court (section 13 Administration of Justice Act 1960)] 9.1 In an appeal under section 13 of the Administration of Justice Act 1960 (appeals in cases of contempt of court), the appellant must serve the appellant’s notice on the court or the Upper Tribunal from whose order or decision the appeal is brought in addition to the persons to be served under rule 52.12(3) and in accordance with that rule. ## Appeal from the Court of Protection

## 10.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (1) In this paragraph –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (a) ‘P’ means a person who lacks, or who is alleged to lack, capacity within the meaning of the Mental Capacity Act 2005 to make a decision or decisions in relation to any matter that is subject to an order of the Court of Protection;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (b) ‘the person effecting notification’ means –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (i) the appellant;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (ii) an agent duly appointed by the appellant; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (iii) such other person as the Court of Protection may direct, who is required to notify P in accordance with this paragraph; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (c) ‘final order’ means a decision of the Court of Appeal that finally determines the appeal proceedings before it. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (2) Where P is not a party to the proceedings, unless the Court of Appeal directs otherwise, the person effecting notification must notify P –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (a) that an appellant’s notice has been filed with the Court of Appeal and –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (i) who the appellant is;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (ii) what final order the appellant is seeking;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (iii) what will happen if the Court of Appeal makes the final order sought by the appellant; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (iv) that P may apply under rule 52.25 (Statutory appeals: court’s power to hear any person) by letter for permission to file evidence or make representations at the appeal hearing;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (b) of the final order, the effect of the final order and what steps P can take in relation to it; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (c) of such other events and documents as the Court of Appeal may direct. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (Paragraphs 3.6 to 3.8 of this Practice Direction 52D contain provisions on how a third party can apply for permission to file evidence or make representations at an appeal hearing.)

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (3) The person effecting notification must provide P with the information specified in sub-paragraph (2)–

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (a) within 14 days of the date on which the appellant’s notice was filed with the Court of Appeal;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (b) within 14 days of the date on which the final order was made; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (c) within such time as the Court of Appeal may direct,

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] as the case may be. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (4) The person effecting notification must provide P in person with the information specified in sub-paragraph (2) in a way that is appropriate to P’s circumstances (for example, using simple language, visual aids or any other appropriate means). [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (5) Where P is to be notified as to –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (a) the existence or effect of a document other than the appellant’s notice or final order; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (b) the taking place of an event,

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] the person effecting notification must explain to P –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (i) in the case of a document, what the document is and what effect, if any, it has; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (ii) in the case of an event, what the event is and its relevance to P. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (6) The person effecting notification must, within 7 days of notifying P, file a certificate of notification (form N165) which certifies –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (a) the date on which P was notified; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (b) that P was notified in accordance with this paragraph. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (7) Where the person effecting notification has not notified P in accordance with this paragraph, a certificate of non-notification (form N165) must be filed with the Court of Appeal stating the reason why notification has not been effected. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (8) Where the person effecting notification must file a certificate of non-notification with the Court of Appeal, the certificate must be filed within the following time limits–

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (a) where P is to be notified in accordance with sub-paragraph (2)(a) (appellant’s notice), within 21 days of the appellant’s notice being filed with the Court of Appeal;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (b) where P is to be notified in accordance with sub-paragraph (2)(b) (final order), within 21 days of the final order being made by the Court of Appeal; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (c) where P is to be notified of such other events and documents as may be directed by the Court of Appeal, within such time as the Court of Appeal directs. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (9) The appellant or such other person as the Court of Appeal may direct may apply to the Court of Appeal seeking an order –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (a) dispensing with the requirement to comply with the provisions of this paragraph; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (b) requiring some other person to comply with the provisions of this paragraph. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (10) An application made under sub-paragraph (9) may be made in the appellant’s notice or by Part 23 application notice. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 10.1] (Paragraphs 6.1 to 6.3 of Practice Direction 52A contain provisions about the dismissal of applications or appeals by consent. Paragraph 6.5 of Practice Direction 52A contains provisions about allowing unopposed appeals or applications involving a child or protected party.)

## Appeal from Employment Appeal Tribunal

## 11.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 11.1] (1) This paragraph applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal from the Employment Appeal Tribunal (EAT) under section 37 of the Employment Tribunals Act 1996. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 11.1] (2) If an application for permission to appeal to the Court of Appeal is refused by the EAT or is not made, then such an application must be made to the Court of Appeal within 21 days of the date of the sealed order of the EAT. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 11.1] (3) An application for extension of time for filing an appellant’s notice may be entertained by the EAT but such applications should normally be made to the Court of Appeal. ## Immigration and Asylum Appeals

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Immigration and Asylum Appeals] 12.1 The provisions of paragraph 28 of Practice Direction 52C (bundle of documents in immigration appeals and asylum appeals) apply to appeals from the Upper Tribunal Immigration and Asylum Chamber. ## Appeal from Patents Court on appeal from Comptroller

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Appeal from Patents Court on appeal from Comptroller] 13.1 Where the appeal is from a decision of the Patents Court which was itself made on an appeal from a decision of the Comptroller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks, the appellant must serve the appellant’s notice on the Comptroller in addition to the persons to be served under rule 52.12(3) and in accordance with that rule. ## Appeal against order for revocation of patent

## 14.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (1) This paragraph applies where an appeal lies to the Court of Appeal from an order for the revocation of a patent. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (2) The appellant must serve the appellant’s notice on the Comptroller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (the ‘Comptroller’) in addition to the persons to be served under rule 52.12(3) and in accordance with that rule. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (3) Where, before the appeal hearing, the respondent decides not to oppose the appeal or not to attend the appeal hearing, the respondent must immediately serve notice of that decision on –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (a) the Comptroller; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (b) the appellant. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (4) Where the respondent serves a notice in accordance with sub-paragraph (3), copies of the following documents must also be served on the Comptroller with that notice –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (a) the petition;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (b) any statements of claim;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (c) any written evidence filed in the claim. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (5) Within 14 days after receiving the notice in accordance with sub-paragraph (3), the Comptroller must serve on the appellant a notice stating an intention to attend the appeal hearing or otherwise. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (6) The Comptroller may attend the appeal hearing and oppose the appeal –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (a) in any case where notice has been given under paragraph (5) of the intention to attend; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 14.1] (b) in any other case (including, in particular, a case where the respondent withdraws his opposition to the appeal during the hearing) if the Court of Appeal so directs or permits. ## Appeal from Proscribed Organisations Appeal Commission

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Appeal from Proscribed Organisations Appeal Commission] 15.1 The appellant’s notice must be filed at the Court of Appeal within 14 days after the date when the Proscribed Organisations Appeal Commission –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Appeal from Proscribed Organisations Appeal Commission] (a) granted; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Appeal from Proscribed Organisations Appeal Commission] (b) where section 6(2)(b) of the Terrorism Act 2000 applies, refused permission to appeal. ## Appeals in relation to serious crime prevention orders

## 16.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 16.1] (1) This paragraph applies to an appeal under section 23(1) of the Serious Crime Act 2007 or section 16 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 in relation to a serious crime prevention order and is made. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 16.1] (2) The appellant must serve the appellant’s notice on any person who made representations in the proceedings by virtue of section 9(1), (2) or (3) of the Serious Crime Act 2007 in addition to the persons to be served under rule 52.12(3) and in accordance with that rule. ## Appeal from Special Immigration Appeals Commission

## 17.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.1] (1) An application for permission to appeal to the Court of Appeal must first be made to the Special Immigration Appeals Commission pursuant section 7(2) of the Special Immigration Appeals Commission Act 1997 and paragraph 27 of the SIAC (Procedure) Rules 2003 (as amended). [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.1] (2) The appellant’s notice must be filed at the Court of Appeal within 21 days of the date on which the Special Immigration Appeals Commission’s decision granting or refusing permission to appeal to the Court of Appeal is given. ## Appeal from Investigatory Powers Tribunal

## 17.2

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.2] (1) An application for leave to appeal to the Court of Appeal must first be made to the Investigatory Powers Tribunal pursuant to rule 16(1) of the Investigatory Powers Tribunal Rules 2018. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.2] (2) The appellant’s notice must be filed at the Court of Appeal within 21 days of the date on which the Investigatory Powers Tribunal’s decision granting or refusing leave to appeal to the Court of Appeal is given. ## 17.3

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.3] (1) The target timescale for determining an application for permission to appeal in a  nationally significant infrastructure project appeal is four weeks from the filing of an appellant’s notice. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.3] (2) Where permission to appeal is sought in a nationally significant infrastructure project appeal—

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.3] (a) the appellant’s notice is to be filed within seven days of the decision being

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.3] appealed;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.3] (b) the appellant’s notice and appellant’s skeleton argument are to be served on the respondent within seven days of the appellant’s notice being sealed;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.3] (c) the appellant is to file a core bundle and serve a core bundle index on the respondent within seven days of the appellant’s notice being sealed; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 17.3] (d) the respondent may file and serve reasons why permission to appeal should not be granted, if so advised, within seven days of service of the appellant’s notice  and appellant’s skeleton argument.
